title: Double operations that overflow give `±inf`
description: No double operation raises "Overflow": every one whose result is too large for a double gives `inf` or `-inf`, from finite inputs: `1e308 * 10`, `1e308 + 1e308`, `-1e308 - 1e308`, `1e308 / 1e-10`, `power(10, 400)`, `10.0 ** 400`, `exp(1000)` (`exp(709.0)` is finite), `sinh(1000)`, `cosh(1000)`, `gamma(200)`, `lgamma(1e308)`, `degrees(1e308)`, and `power(0, -1)`.
Aggregates too: `sum` and `avg` of `1e308` and `1e308` are `inf`, grouped and over a window; `fsum` of them is NaN; `var_pop` of `1e308` and `-1e308` is `-inf`.
A cast of a double outside `FLOAT`'s range to `FLOAT` raises a conversion error, the one overflow that raises.

`FLOAT` arithmetic overflows the same way, in single precision: `3e38::FLOAT + 3e38::FLOAT`, `* 10` and `/ 1e-3` are `inf`, `-3e38 - 3e38` is `-inf`, and the result stays `FLOAT`. `sum` and `avg` of `FLOAT` accumulate and return a `DOUBLE` (duckdb-float-sum-order), so `sum` of `3e38` and `3e38` is the finite 6.0000000109955115e+38; grouped, `sum` and `avg` of `1e308` and `1e308` are `inf`.
The docs are silent on the DOUBLE-to-FLOAT conversion error: a docs gap. No upstream test pins it; it may change between versions.
reference: An operation on finite doubles whose result is `±inf` raises (`Issue.infinite`, #575): an inferred precondition the written plan checks on the data (`CASE WHEN … THEN error('overflow to infinity')`), as for a `SUM` that leaves 64 bits. Under D25 (#915) the reference's `AVG` is the exact mean rounded once, so `AVG` of `1e308` and `1e308` is `1e308` there, where DuckDB's running sum overflows to `inf`: its guarded plan raises (`overflow to infinity`), which the reference allows, and the unguarded replay disagrees (`overflow/test_numeric_overflow.test:39`, `characterization/duckdb/overflow.json`).

evidence.sql: SELECT 1e308::DOUBLE * 10, 1e308::DOUBLE + 1e308::DOUBLE, 1e308::DOUBLE / 1e-10::DOUBLE, power(10::DOUBLE, 400::DOUBLE), exp(1000::DOUBLE), exp(709.0::DOUBLE), sinh(1000::DOUBLE), gamma(200::DOUBLE), degrees(1e308::DOUBLE), power(0::DOUBLE, -1::DOUBLE)
evidence.observed: inf, inf, inf, inf, inf, 8.218407461554972e+307, inf, inf, inf, inf

evidence.sql: SELECT sum(x), avg(x), fsum(x) FROM (VALUES (1e308::DOUBLE), (1e308::DOUBLE)) t(x)

evidence.observed: Conversion Error: Type DOUBLE with value 1e+308 can't be cast because the value is out of range for the destination type FLOAT

provenance.notes: Run one statement at a time on an in-memory connection with the default settings (`ieee_floating_point_ops` on).

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline session (float_overflow rows), duckdb Python 2.0.0

evidence.sql: SELECT sum(x), avg(x), typeof(sum(x)), typeof(avg(x)) FROM (VALUES (3e38::FLOAT), (3e38::FLOAT)) t(x)
SELECT g, sum(x), avg(x) FROM (VALUES (1, 1e308::DOUBLE), (1, 1e308::DOUBLE)) t(g, x) GROUP BY g

provenance.notes: One statement at a time on an in-memory connection with the default settings.

evidence.note: float/double +: C++ operator, no overflow check
double to float fails when a finite value becomes infinite: the one raising overflow
out-of-range values usually become zero or infinity
DOUBLE and FLOAT +, -, *, / past the range → ±inf
